scope: Seven Batch2 decisions; review-only. No canonical pages, admissions, public components or SEC registry changes.
rubric: Existing provisional D/B/P/R appraisal convention; no new anchors, caps or admission thresholds. Calibration proposal not promoted into new policy.
reconciliation: Local completed discovery manifest/register used, including pre-existing uncommitted work. PM1 saved source appraisal reused. Discovery completion does not imply SEC completion. Canonical current registry has65 PMs following separately authorised CoQ addition; no discovery rerun.
sourceEditorialCheck: Scite metadata for seven papers returned no editorialNotices field; a retraction-filter query returned no matching hits, not proof of a clean literature record. Bruno linked commentary identified and remains to be appraised. No adverse notice was affirmatively identified in inspected primary records.

records.proposition: In the pooled Maastricht tracer dataset, whey was associated with earlier dietary phenylalanine appearance and a larger five-hour circulating fraction than micellar casein; this is not an isolated causal comparison across otherwise identical protocols.
records.studyContext: Pooled 18 laboratory RCT datasets, 602 people (590 men); whey n=137, casein n=393, milk n=72. Mean protein doses 23±5, 24±7 and 26±11 g, respectively. Intrinsically labelled protein plus intravenous tracer; ANOVA with Bonferroni comparisons. Trials differed in dose, age, time of day and co-interventions.
records.admissionRationale: PM fit is established for meal-level circulating provision, but a reproducible matched whey-versus-casein practice should be extracted from constituent trials before turning the pooled contrast into an intervention recommendation. Do not reject merely because brain delivery was unmeasured.
records.mainLimitation: Pooled interstudy contrast; no single matched protocol or universal whey advantage.
records.implementationStatus: Review only; no canonical admission, assessment pin or presentation changed

limitations.text: Milk had greater five-hour appearance than whey; fastest appearance is not greatest total delivery.
Casein appearance continues beyond five hours; lower five-hour fraction is not total protein loss.
Predominantly men; age and co-interventions differ across contributing studies.
Phenylalanine tracer appearance is not brain uptake, neurotransmitter synthesis or cognitive benefit.

rationale.D: Tracer appearance directly measures the precisely stated circulating-source comparison; D2 does not apply to brain supply or a causal superiority claim.
rationale.B: Standardised tracer programme and multiplicity controls, but pooled protein groups differ in participant and protocol characteristics; the descriptive proposition is retained rather than causal attribution.
rationale.P: 57±10% whey versus 45±11% casein, reported P<0.001; heterogeneity and a finite five-hour window limit transferable magnitude.
rationale.R: One pooled analytical evidence line. Eighteen source trials are not automatically eighteen replications of this exact source contrast; independent matched comparison has not been appraised.

sourceVerification.level: Saved full-primary appraisal reused and primary body cross-checked
sourceVerification.newVerification: Scite fulltext body through Methods, Results, Discussion and figure captions; no SF score inherited

moa.description: Protein structure and digestion/absorption kinetics may contribute to source differences; splanchnic extraction also influences systemic appearance. This pooled analysis does not isolate causal mediation.

biologicalRelationship.measuredEffect: Five-hour fraction: whey 57±10%, casein 45±11%, milk 65±13%. Peak timing whey 49±20 versus casein 96±72 minutes.
biologicalRelationship.pmRelevance: Meal-level amino-acid provision is explicitly owned by PM1.

records.existingRecordCheck: Gorissen already supports PM1-F1. Current SOPs are minced beef and boiled eggs, with separate SEC pins; neither is this source comparison.
records.mission: Ensure meal-level protein supply delivers the amino-acid foundation neurotransmitter pathways depend on.

existingSops.input: Minced rather than intact beef in the tested older-adult meal
Boiled rather than raw eggs in the tested postexercise meal

records.intervention: Vitamin C supplementation and vitamin E retention
records.proposition: Two weeks of vitamin C attenuated plasma labelled alpha- and gamma-tocopherol fractional disappearance in smokers, without an observed reduction in plasma F2-isoprostanes.
records.studyContext: Abstract: randomised double-blind placebo-controlled crossover; 11 smokers and 13 nonsmokers; ascorbate 500 mg twice daily for two weeks, single 50 mg doses of each labelled tocopheryl acetate.
records.admissionRationale: Relevant retention endpoint and established chemical recycling relationship, but original bias protections, kinetic uncertainty and published critique remain incompletely appraised. Not a demonstrated recycling-flux or general antioxidant-benefit protocol.
records.mainLimitation: Primary methods unavailable; retention is not direct radical-recycling flux.

sourceVerification.comment: Hemilä 2007, DOI 10.1016/j.freeradbiomed.2006.11.035, identified by PubMed as a comment, not a retraction; title concerns surrogate endpoints. Full comment and author reply not appraised.

moa.description: Ascorbate reduction of tocopheroxyl radicals is established chemically, but the human experiment infers recycling from slower disappearance.

biologicalRelationship.measuredEffect: Abstract reports 25% and 45% slower fractional disappearance in smokers; no corresponding effect in nonsmokers.
biologicalRelationship.pmRelevance: Antioxidant regeneration is PM6’s operation; retention is a related endpoint, not direct regeneration flux.

records.existingRecordCheck: Vitamin C and vitamin E are already dietary inputs; PM6-F1 is chemical recycling evidence. No active SOP or intervention SEC pin for Bruno found.

records.intervention: Defined prebiotic blend and circulating indolepropionate
records.proposition: The tested 12-g/day blend for four weeks increased the plasma indolepropionate metabolomic signal relative to its matched placebo in healthy low-fibre consumers.
records.studyContext: 24 randomised, 20 completed (10 men/10 women), ages 18–45, habitual fibre<15 g/day; double-blind crossover, four-week arms and four-week washout. Blend: FOS, resistant starch, sugarcane fibre, inulin, gum arabic, xanthan gum, apple/raspberry/blueberry powders. Placebo: rice flour, xanthan gum, grape/plum powders. UHPLC-MS metabolomics; treatment×time+subject models.
records.admissionRationale: PM8 already owns microbial tryptophan processing, including indole routes. The signal is relevant, but exact ingredient proportions/material specification are not supplied in the inspected article, and the marginal secondary endpoint needs qualification. Do not substitute generic inulin, fibre or whole fruit.
records.mainLimitation: Unadjusted secondary IPA result (P=0.04); formulation specificity and concentration-versus-flux boundary.
records.implementationStatus: Review only; no canonical admission, assessment pin or presentation changed

limitations.text: No significant change in TMAO (P=0.84), fecal SCFAs, overall microbial diversity, cardiometabolic profiles or bowel movement measures.
IPA hypothesised in paper but secondary; Figure4 reports unadjusted P-values. Other exploratory taxa/pathway signals did not survive correction.
12 g is packet/blend mass, not a verified 12 g of pure fibre; constituent proportions not recovered.
Plasma IPA is not direct gut production flux, serotonin supply, brain uptake or health benefit.
20 completers with low habitual fibre intake; four-week exposure.

rationale.D: Exact plasma IPA response to this formulation measured; D2 does not establish microbial production flux or central precursor delivery.
rationale.B: Randomised blinded crossover with diet patterning and washout; four withdrawals, no explicit carryover robustness result located, and multiple secondary readouts.
rationale.P: IPA P=0.04 unadjusted; small cohort, untargeted signal, no clinically interpretable absolute dose-response/CI established. Direction is reported but magnitude remains weakly constrained.
rationale.R: One exact-formulation study. Separate bean-hull bread and broader diet studies in discovery are not replications of this formulation.

sourceVerification.access: Scite fulltext, entire body through final figure captions

moa.description: Substrate-driven changes in microbial tryptophan metabolism are plausible; producer-specific mediation and production rate were not demonstrated.

biologicalRelationship.measuredEffect: Higher plasma IPA metabolomic signal, P=0.04 unadjusted.
biologicalRelationship.pmRelevance: Existing PM8-F1/F3 already cover fibre-dependent microbial tryptophan/indole processing; no mission expansion required.

records.existingRecordCheck: DISC-FIBRE-IPA is preliminary discovery only; no current PM8 SOP or intervention SEC pin. Existing apple-pectin Findings do not establish equivalence to this blend.
records.mission: Maintain gut-side processing that shapes neurotransmitter precursor availability.

records.proposition: In adults with postinfectious IBS-D and elevated baseline urinary lactulose:mannitol ratio, glutamine 5 g three times daily for eight weeks reduced this permeability measure compared with the whey-protein control.
records.studyContext: Two-centre double-blind randomised trial;115 randomised (59/56),106 completers (54/52). Central computer sequence, numbered containers, matched powders; whey protein 5 g three times/day control. Secondary permeability endpoint; primary endpoint IBS symptom-score reduction. Completer analysis.
records.admissionRationale: Recommend only the tested condition-specific protocol and permeability proposition, subject to author approval. It adds a defined intervention to existing glutamine provision, not another dietary input or generic gut-repair claim.
records.mainLimitation: Selected hyperpermeable postinfectious IBS-D; secondary endpoint, completer analysis and whey comparator.
records.implementationStatus: Review only; no canonical admission, assessment pin or presentation changed

limitations.text: 106 completers from115 randomised; narrative withdrawal counts are internally inconsistent. Use flow/Results cohort sizes, not a claim of complete intention-to-treat.
Whey protein is not biologically inert; authors note possible IBS sensitivity. No significant symptom exacerbation was observed in control.
Permeability was secondary; no direct junction-protein or mediator measurement.
Not generalisable to IBS with normal permeability, other disease types, children, pregnancy/lactation or excluded renal/hepatic impairment.
No significant control-arm permeability change; adverse-event rates similar and no serious adverse events reported. Long-term safety not established.
Earlier discovery shorthand0.05 versus0.11 conflated post-treatment with active-group baseline; post-treatment control was0.10, and Table3 is the actual between-group change comparison.

rationale.D: Urinary lactulose:mannitol is the exact assessed permeability endpoint and fits the PM’s selective permeability operation. No tight-junction protein change asserted.
rationale.B: Computer allocation, matching, masking and independent analysis documented; completer-only analysis, physiologically active whey comparator and inconsistent withdrawal prose prevent full bias credit.
rationale.P: Table3 reports change -0.06±0.03 versus -0.0004±0.03 (means±SD;54/52), P<0.0001. Uncertainty resolves the prespecified-for-this-appraisal directional proposition (reduction vs no reduction); no clinical-importance threshold or generalisable effect size is inferred.
rationale.R: One exact condition/protocol dataset; two recruitment sites are not independent replicated trials. Other disease/cell studies are mechanistic context, not exact replication.

sourceVerification.level: Full primary body and tables inspected
sourceVerification.access: Scite fulltext Methods/Results/Discussion; PMC9549483 Tables2/3 checked separately because indexed text omitted table cells. BioC request returned429; HTML tables accessible.
sourceVerification.bibliographicNote: Online2018; journal issue2019. Same trial, not two studies.

moa.description: Glutamine may support epithelial metabolism and junction maintenance; correlations with symptom changes do not prove causal mediation and junction proteins were not measured.

biologicalRelationship.measuredEffect: L:M baseline0.11±0.03 to0.05±0.01 on glutamine; control0.11±0.04 to0.10±0.03. Between-group change test P<0.0001.
biologicalRelationship.pmRelevance: Selective gut permeability is directly within PM1 mission; no ADHD inference.

records.existingRecordCheck: PM1-F6 already includes this trial and glutamine has an accepted dietary atom. Current sole SOP is fat with provitamin-A vegetables. No glutamine protocol SEC pin found; do not inherit F6 score.
records.mission: Maintain epithelial tight junction integrity and selective permeability at the gut lining.

existingSops.input: Include dietary fat with provitamin-A vegetables

records.proposition: In the tested acute crossover, an egg-yolk phospholipid drink providing3 g choline produced a greater six-hour plasma free-choline response than a choline-bitartrate drink supplying the same choline dose.
records.studyContext: 18 healthy adults(7 men,11 women;mean 62.3 years), randomised double-blind crossover, one-week washout;37 g freeze-dried ELIP egg phospholipids versus 9.3 g choline bitartrate, each equivalent 3 g choline. Shared juice,whey and maltodextrin base; lipid matrices differ. Samples 0–360 min; UPLC-MS/MS; paired iAUC and mixed models.
records.admissionRationale: Recommend only a bounded experimental choline-provision SOP through the already accepted PM6-DIT-2/PM6-F4 route. No whole-egg equivalence, routine3-g prescription or demonstrated acetylcholine effect. Do not also assign it to BRS2-PM7 as proof of phosphatidylcholine synthesis.
records.mainLimitation: High-dose phospholipid concentrate; circulating choline, not neuronal uptake or acetylcholine.
records.implementationStatus: Review only; no canonical admission, assessment pin or presentation changed

limitations.text: Single3-g choline challenge, not ordinary egg consumption or a daily dose recommendation; lower-dose effect may differ.
No plasma phospholipid-DHA response; no between-drink TAG-DHA difference after dose correction. Do not claim DHA superiority.
Faecal-consistency changes reported more often with phospholipid drink; not long-term tolerability evidence.
Plasma concentration/iAUC is not measured absorption fraction, brain choline, acetylcholine synthesis or cognition.
37 g isolated egg phospholipids in a defined drink, not37 g egg yolk; whole-food equivalence untested.
Specific causal mediator unresolved; omit a collapsed mechanism summary pending adequate identification.

rationale.D: Exact drink-to-plasma-choline proposition directly measured. PM relevance is separately bounded upstream substrate provision, not a scored acetylcholine response.
rationale.B: Randomised blinded within-person comparison, standardised preceding meals and washout; small commercial-formulation study, different matrices and no independent validation of all allocation/prospective analysis protections.
rationale.P: Fourfold six-hour choline iAUC response, P<0.01, with participant consistency and reported variability; small high-dose sample limits magnitude and lower-dose extrapolation.
rationale.R: One exact formulation/dose comparison. Earlier lecithin/choline-chloride and lower-dose whole-egg studies cited by authors were not independently appraised as matching replications.

sourceVerification.access: Scite fulltext through Methods, Results, Discussion and limitations

moa.description: Phospholipid digestion and transport differ from free-choline salt handling. The authors could only speculate on why plasma response differed; saturation at the high dose remains possible.

biologicalRelationship.measuredEffect: Approximately fourfold choline iAUC versus bitartrate; betaine and dimethylglycine responses also higher.
biologicalRelationship.pmRelevance: Existing PM6-F4 and dietary atom PM6-DIT-2 explicitly accept dietary phosphatidylcholine-to-circulating-choline provision. Contract allows connected proximal effects when kept separate from PM activity.

records.existingRecordCheck: Choline and phosphatidylcholine already admitted in PM6; no SOP entries. BRS2-FM3-PM7 duplicate discovery lead inspected: neither Kennedy nor PEMT synthesis was measured, so no additional assignment recommended.
records.mission: Maintain the capacity to form acetylcholine so cholinergic signalling for attention, working memory, and learning stays supplied.

records.proposition: The three-month high-flavanol drink increased dentate-gyrus cerebral blood volume and improved the specified ModBent reaction-time endpoint; human synapse formation or structural remodelling was not measured.
records.studyContext: Healthy sedentary adults 50–69;37 completed four-group flavanol×exercise experiment;900 versus 10 mg flavanols/day, with/without exercise. CBV-fMRI and cognitive task.
records.admissionRationale: Reject this human vascular/cognitive result as a demonstrated synaptic-structural SOP for PM12. Preserve it as contextual evidence. Mouse spine work cited in the introduction is a separate study and cannot be silently substituted for the human endpoint.
records.mainLimitation: Cerebral blood volume is not a human synaptic structural endpoint.
records.implementationStatus: Review only; no canonical admission, assessment pin or presentation changed

limitations.text: Delayed retention did not improve; exercise showed no significant cognitive or VO2max effect in this trial.
Cited mouse dendritic-spine study is separate evidence, not a measured structural result in these humans.
Reject concerns receiving-PM intervention claim, not the validity of the measured vascular/cognitive observations.

sourceVerification.level: Targeted primary-text eligibility verification, not full SEC appraisal
sourceVerification.access: Scite Introduction and Results, including High flavanol intake improves DG function.

records.existingRecordCheck: No cocoa SOP in current PM12. Existing DHA–UMP, spermidine, active-period feeding and magnesium protocols are distinct. No alternate PM invented.

moa.description: The human study motivates a structural inference from prior separate animal observations; CBV/cognition cannot identify synaptic remodelling.

biologicalRelationship.measuredEffect: DG CBV increased; ModBent reaction time differed by630 ms; no delayed-retention benefit.
biologicalRelationship.pmRelevance: PM12 owns physical synapse formation/stabilisation/remodelling, not a generic cerebral vascular or memory endpoint.

records.mission: Maintain and adapt physical connections between neurons through synapse formation, selective stabilisation, structural remodelling and elimination.

records.proposition: After16 weeks, matched average EPA+DHA provision from fish or capsules increased red-cell EPA+DHA in both arms without a significant group effect.
records.studyContext: Healthy premenopausal women;fish n=11,capsules n=12;average 485 mg/day EPA+DHA via two weekly salmon/albacore-tuna servings or 1–2 capsules/day. Blood-cell and plasma-phospholipid fatty acids.
records.admissionRationale: Retain as peripheral exposure/source context; no fish-over-capsule optimisation advantage demonstrated. Decide whether an alternatives-only provision practice adds a distinct PM-specific purpose beyond existing DHA admission before full SEC appraisal. Lack of a brain endpoint alone does not prohibit an explicitly bounded supply relationship.
records.mainLimitation: Red-cell EPA+DHA composite, not neuronal DHA; nonsignificance is not demonstrated equivalence.
records.implementationStatus: Review only; no canonical admission, assessment pin or presentation changed

limitations.text: No significant overall group effect; equal endpoint means are not a formal equivalence/noninferiority test.
Headline result is combined EPA+DHA, not DHA alone.
Small cohort of healthy premenopausal women; cannot inherit older-adult CNS results.
No automatic supplement/food equivalence in brain delivery.

sourceVerification.access: PubMed18065578; Scite metadata fulltext contentDenied=true. Full SEC retrieval not pursued after uncertain gate.

records.existingRecordCheck: PM7 already admits DHA and has PM7-SOP-DHA-1 for a defined older-adult low-intake protocol with different evidence. Fish/capsules is not already that protocol and must not duplicate it under a new label.

moa.description: Both sources deliver fatty acids to blood lipid pools; comparative neuronal incorporation was not studied.

biologicalRelationship.measuredEffect: RBC EPA+DHA reached6.2% in both groups; early RBC EPA rise faster with fish, later group rates not significantly different.
biologicalRelationship.pmRelevance: PM7 owns neuronal membrane DHA integration; peripheral provision relevance is plausible but comparative protocol purpose and endpoint distance remain unresolved.

records.mission: Deliver and integrate DHA into neuronal membranes so the brain maintains a flexible, signal-ready lipid foundation.

existingSops.input: Defined DHA supplementation in older adults with low baseline DHA intake
